title: Deciding What of the Supplement's Payments on Lines Outside Cover Reached the Policyholder Herself
content:
On a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies, what of the money paid on lines outside cover reached the policyholder herself is settled from how those lines came to the supplement and what they record her owing.

1. **Where lines outside cover were submitted by the policyholder herself** — what reached her is taken as what the supplement paid on those lines.
2. **Where no line outside cover was submitted by her, but lines outside cover record her owing nothing at all** — what reached her is taken as what the supplement paid on those lines, she having already settled with the provider.
3. **Where neither of those holds** — nothing is treated as having reached her.

### Reading the three cases

The first case turns on a single fact: that lines outside cover were submitted by the policyholder herself. Where any were, what the supplement paid on them is what reached her.

The second case is reached only where she submitted none of the lines outside cover. It then requires that those lines record her owing nothing at all; a line outside cover recording her owing any amount takes the record out of this case.

Where she submitted none of the lines outside cover and those lines record her owing something, nothing is treated as having reached her.

### Hypothetical records

Lines outside cover she submitted herself, on which the supplement paid 210.00: 210.00 reached her.

No line outside cover submitted by her, and the lines outside cover record her owing nothing at all, the supplement having paid 96.00 on them: 96.00 reached her.

No line outside cover submitted by her, and those lines record her owing 40.00: nothing is treated as having reached her.
